alternatives.option: Keep pre-create flip, add a second post-create updateStatus for the back-link
alternatives.reason_rejected: Two lock acquisitions and two export-tree writes per supersede, and keeps the create-throws-after-flip inconsistency.

assumptions: The engine decide() path is the only supersede write site (override() routes through decide(); record-tools passes supersedes into decide()) — grep for updateStatus(..."superseded") confirms no other caller.
Housekeeping loading every decision file for the scan is acceptable at field scale (staleness review already does the same).
constraints: No plugin/ changes (adoption surface shipped in plugin 1.24.1)
No commits, no version bumps, no CHANGELOG edits from this worktree
Keep decisions.ts and housekeeping.ts diffs modular — teammates crosspost-30 and archive-35 are editing the same files concurrently
context: Fixed #31 server half: superseded_by back-links now written at supersede time in both backends, surfaced by twining_why, and backfilled for historical decisions by a new housekeeping pass. TDD, 1075 tests green, build/typecheck clean.
rationale: The replacement id does not exist until create returns, so a pre-create back-link is impossible without pre-generating ids (invasive store change) or double-writing (two locks, two export-tree writes). Post-create also fixes a latent inconsistency: previously, if create threw, the old decision was left superseded with no successor. The conflict-filter exclusion (entry.id !== input.supersedes) preserves the prior behavior where the already-flipped target never appeared as a conflict.
summary: Moved the supersede status flip in DecisionEngine.decide from before create to after create, writing status and superseded_by in one updateStatus call; conflict scan now excludes the supersede target
